title: seed kickoff: llm integration sprint notes + quickstart blueprint (draft)
content:
Overview
---
Quick working notes from the seed kickoff sprint for a CLI-guided labs + quickstart blueprint aimed at making first-10-minutes success for engineers embedding LLM features. This is a sketchy, iteration-first doc — expect TODOs and questions. Meant to become a short, runnable repo + CLI recipe that product-engineers can run locally or in sandboxed cloud accounts.

Goals
- Create a 5–8 minute CLI-first quickstart that: provisions a sandbox API key, scaffolds a minimal app, runs a smoke generation, and shows how to read latency/cost breakdowns.
- Include 3 hands-on lab scenarios (classification, chat assistant, semantic search) that exercise SDK patterns and failure modes.
- Produce a short checklist and rollout gating recommendations for eng/product teams.

Audience
- Primary: internal engineers and early adopter customers using Redwood API and SDKs.
- Secondary: solutions engineers running demos and customer POCs.

Principles
- Minimal friction: 1–2 typed commands to get to a working example.
- Observable by default: quick links to Console traces / token cost summary printed by CLI.
- Safe defaults: small context windows, sampling defaults, and test-mode key creation.
- Reproducible: deterministic example prompts and seed outputs for eval harness.

Quickstart CLI flow (sketch)
1) Install: npm i -g @redwood/cli || pipx install redwood-cli
2) redwood login --sandbox (opens browser OAuth or prints ephemeral key)
3) redwood init --template starter-chat --name "ticket-buddy"
   - scaffolds node/py app, adds README with commands
4) cd ticket-buddy && redwood run --smoke
   - runs local invocation against hosted sandbox endpoint, prints: model, tokens, ms latency, cost (estimated)
5) redwood inspect --trace recent
   - prints short trace + URL to Console trace view

Notes on UX: the init command should ask a single branching question: "Do you want chat / classification / embeddings?" then scaffold the appropriate example with tests.

Example: Node quick snippet (to appear in README)
- code block (inline):
const { Redwood } = require('@redwood/sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
(async ()=>{
  const r = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-chat-1', messages: [{role:'user', content:'Summarize sales notes'}] });
  console.log(r.choices[0].message.content);
})();

Example: Python quick snippet
from redwood import Redwood
client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
print(client.chat.create(model='redwood-chat-1', messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain the changes in Q1"}]))

Lab scenarios (3) — short outlines
1) Intent-classification pipeline (30–45 min)
- scaffold a small CLI that takes CSV of utterances, runs batch embeddings + light classifier, shows cost per batch and suggestions for batching settings.
- failure mode lab: embedding dimension mismatch, rate limit handling, retry/backoff heuristics.

2) Assistive-chat demo (40–60 min)
- build a local assistant that calls chat with function/tool calling for calendar lookup (mocked). Includes an example of streaming output and a fallback to shorter model for degraded connections.
- observability tasks: show per-request token breakdown and a trace showing where latency spiked.

3) Semantic search + QA (45 min)
- ingest a short docset (markdown), create embeddings, store locally in lightweight vector DB (we will provide a small in-repo SQLite+HNSW script). Run a question -> retrieval -> answer pipeline. Show how to tune chunk size and embedding model for cost/quality tradeoffs.

Experiment matrix (what to measure in the sprint)
- First-run success rate (target >85% for internal testers)
- Time-to-first-response (target <8min including install)
- Median tokens and cost per example for each lab scenario
- Error types surfaced (auth errors, rate limit, env misconfig)
- Net promoter rating from 10 test users (quick survey)

Telemetry / metrics to surface in quickstart
- show a single JSON blob printed at end of smoke test with: model, tokens_in, tokens_out, ms_latency_p50/p95, estimated_cost_usd
- provide `redwood diag` that formats and optionally uploads results to a private trace for deeper analysis (opt-in)

Rollout gating / priming for docs + SDK changes
- docs: must include a 1-page quickstart cheat sheet, the detailed lab README, and a short troubleshooting page.
- SDK: minimal breaking surface — prefer wrappers that call existing clients.
- QA gating: smoke tests pass and at least 3 internal devs run quickstart without prompting.

Checklist (todo for next week)
- [ ] finalize CLI flags and UX copy (Priya)
- [ ] create starter repo skeleton + templates for three labs (Ethan)
- [ ] add cost telemetry payload and Console link printing (Lena)
- [ ] write the 1-page quickstart cheat sheet + immutable example prompts (Marcus)
- [ ] record 3 short screencast gifs for README landing page (engineer volunteer)

Open questions / risks (notes to self)
- Do we allow `redwood login --sandbox` to create ephemeral keys without org-level consent? legal/privacy check needed. (ask security)
- How large should the example dataset be for semantic search so that it is useful but cheap? 5–10 small markdown files seems right.
- Should the CLI auto-run `redwood optimize suggest` and print recommendations after smoke? Might be noisy for first-run.

Small UX experiments to try during sprint
- inline opt-out: when printing Console trace URLs, show a short human-readable summary in terminal to avoid clicking.
- provide `--no-network` local-mode that runs a fake local model for pure offline demos (useful for customer workshops).

References & links (internal)
- Quick reference to GitHub PR with template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/pull/412
- Related ticket: JIRA-ENG-987 (seed quickstart epic)
